answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only after a peer has vouched for them through repeated, independently verified exchanges. Each vouch is backed by a small stake that is forfeited if later audits uncover fabricated work; trust therefore grows from costly history, not from creating more accounts. A falcon may spot a lotus on a ledge, but an attacker cannot multiply identities to multiply credibility: they must fund each account and risk losing its stake, while still earning real attestations over time.
